neighbours.label: the verb at the end of a comparative clause after 'than' with its own subject (more energy than it consumes, prettier than it looks)
fire: This engine burns more fuel than it needs on short trips.
The old bridge is far weaker than it appears from the road.
Our farm grows more wheat than we can sell at the market.
He owes more money than he earns in a whole year.
The salad tasted better than it sounds on the menu.
Her essay is longer than it should be for this class.
The company spends more on rent than it makes in sales.
They caught more fish than they could carry back to camp.
quiet: This engine burns diesel and it needs oil on short trips.
The old bridge is rusty, and it appears on many postcards.
Our farm grows wheat that we can sell at the market.
He owes money and he earns very little in a whole year.
The salad tasted fresh and it sounds cheap on the menu.
Her essay is long and it should be fine for this class.
The company pays its rent because it makes steady sales.
They caught fish that they could carry back to camp.

notes: Card: could, have, can, is, consumes, uses, looks: every peak ends a comparative clause, with one French parallel. Probes: 'than it consumes' 1.483, 'than it looks' 0.873, 'than he could count' 0.561; the same verbs in coordinated clauses under 0.02. Near misses keep the verbs and drop 'than'.
